LESSON: MASS, VOLUME, WEIGHT AND DENSITY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.2 Volume of Solids (8 lessons) • Volume of triangular and rectang
Topic 3.3: Mass, Volume, Weight and Density

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Mass, Volume, Weight and Density. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do you weigh materials and objects?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. convert units of mass from one form to another in different situations
2. relate mass and weight in real-life situations
3. determine mass volume, and density of different substances

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Mass, Volume, Weight and Density.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Mass, Volume, Weight and Density using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Discuss different instruments and tools used in weighing materials or objects and relate them to consumer awareness and protection.
2. Discuss the relationship between mass and weight.
3. Carry out activities relating mass and volume to density using containers or different substances.
4. Discuss and find the density of different materials or objects.
5. Communication and Collaboration: learner discusses the relationship between mass and weight.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Mass, Volume, Weight and Density is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
